title: Impact of Unexpected Dovish Fed Announcements on Bank Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event study using the market model.
- Why: A single, market-wide, unanticipated policy shock occurs at event_day = 0 for all banks. Event studies isolate the immediate impact by comparing realized returns to a model-implied “normal” return estimated from the pre-event window.
- Key assumptions:
  - The dovish announcement is an unanticipated shock (no information leakage).
  - No confounding, concurrent events systematically affecting bank stocks at the same time.
  - The market model is correctly specified over the short window: E[ret_it] = alpha_i + beta_i*mkt_ret_t with stable beta_i around the event.
  - Short-window inference: abnormal returns are not contaminated by other risk premia, and cross-firm dependence is limited enough for cross-sectional t-tests to be informative.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
})

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s60_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))

# 2) Estimate normal returns (alpha_i) from pre-event window using provided beta_i
#    alpha_i = mean(ret - beta_i * mkt_ret) over event_day < 0
alpha_df <- df %>%
  filter(event_day < 0) %>%
  mutate(ar_pre = ret - beta * mkt_ret) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(alpha = mean(ar_pre, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_pre = sum(!is.na(ar_pre)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_pre > 0) %>%
  select(stock_id, alpha)

# Merge alpha back and compute abnormal returns (AR) under the market model
df_ar <- df %>%
  inner_join(alpha_df, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(AR = ret - alpha - beta * mkt_ret,
         # Robustness alternative: market-adjusted abnormal returns
         AR_MA = ret - mkt_ret)

# Helper: compute CAR by window and t-test against zero
car_window <- function(data, L, H, ar_col = "AR") {
  tmp <- data %>%
    filter(event_day >= L, event_day <= H) %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    summarise(CAR = sum(.data[[ar_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
              n_days = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_days > 0)

  N <- nrow(tmp)
  if (N == 0) return(list(N = 0, meanCAR = NA, sdCAR = NA, se = NA, t = NA, p = NA))
  meanCAR <- mean(tmp$CAR)
  sdCAR   <- sd(tmp$CAR)
  se      <- sdCAR / sqrt(N)
  tstat   <- ifelse(is.finite(se) && se > 0, meanCAR / se, NA_real_)
  pval    <- ifelse(is.finite(tstat), 2 * pt(-abs(tstat), df = N - 1), NA_real_)
  list(N = N, meanCAR = meanCAR, sdCAR = sdCAR, se = se, t = tstat, p = pval)
}

fmt <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 4, format = "f")

# 3) Baseline event windows (immediate reaction)
res_00 <- car_window(df_ar, 0, 0, "AR")   # Day 0 only
res_01 <- car_window(df_ar, 0, 1, "AR")   # [0, +1]
res_02 <- car_window(df_ar, 0, 2, "AR")   # [0, +2]

# 4) Robustness checks
# 4a) Market-adjusted returns (ignore alpha and beta), window [0, +1]
res_01_MA <- car_window(df_ar, 0, 1, "AR_MA")

# 4b) Placebo pre-event CAR, window [-5, -1], should be ~0
res_placebo <- car_window(df_ar, -5, -1, "AR")

# 5) Print results
cat("Event Study: Impact of Unexpected Dovish Fed Announcement on Bank Stock CAR\n")
cat("Units (stocks) used:", res_01$N, "\n\n")

cat("Baseline Market-Model CARs (alpha_i from pre-event, given beta_i):\n")
cat("  CAR[0,0]:  mean =", fmt(res_00$meanCAR), 
    ", t =", fmt(res_00$t), ", p =", fmt(res_00$p), 
    ", N =", res_00$N, "\n", sep = "")
cat("  CAR[0,1]:  mean =", fmt(res_01$meanCAR), 
    ", t =", fmt(res_01$t), ", p =", fmt(res_01$p), 
    ", N =", res_01$N, "\n", sep = "")
cat("  CAR[0,2]:  mean =", fmt(res_02$meanCAR), 
    ", t =", fmt(res_02$t), ", p =", fmt(res_02$p), 
    ", N =", res_02$N, "\n\n", sep = "")

cat("Robustness:\n")
cat("  Market-Adjusted (ret - mkt_ret) CAR[0,1]: mean =", fmt(res_01_MA$meanCAR), 
    ", t =", fmt(res_01_MA$t), ", p =", fmt(res_01_MA$p),
    ", N =", res_01_MA$N, "\n", sep = "")
cat("  Placebo CAR[-5,-1] (should be ~0): mean =", fmt(res_placebo$meanCAR),
    ", t =", fmt(res_placebo$t), ", p =", fmt(res_placebo$p),
    ", N =", res_placebo$N, "\n", sep = "")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Slightly negative abnormal performance for banks on a dovish surprise after controlling for market movement, because lower policy rates compress net interest margins and banks typically underperform the market on such news.
- Magnitude: CAR[0,1] around -0.3% to -0.8%, concentrated on day 0; CAR[0,0] roughly -0.2% to -0.5%; CAR[0,2] similar or slightly larger in absolute value if effects persist.
- Robustness: Market-adjusted CARs should show a similar sign. The placebo window [-5, -1] should be statistically indistinguishable from zero.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare bank stock returns around the event day to assess the impact of the announcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Unexpected dovish Fed announcements lead to a decrease in bank stock CAR.
